title: Heaps, Greedy, Tries & Monotonic Stacks
description: Priority queues, greedy proofs, prefix trees, and monotonic stacks — the patterns behind top-K, scheduling, autocomplete, and next-greater problems.
longDescription: These four structures and techniques cover a large share of 'medium' and 'hard' interview problems and rarely appear in a basic algorithms curriculum. A heap solves top-K and scheduling problems in O(n log k) instead of a full sort. Greedy reasoning solves interval and jump problems where local choices are provably correct. A trie turns prefix lookups into O(length) walks. A monotonic stack answers 'next greater element' style questions in a single pass. Each lesson contrasts the naive approach with the optimal one and explains why the optimisation is valid.
whatYouLearn: Choosing between a full sort and a heap of size k
Scheduling with a priority queue and a cooldown counter
Proving a greedy choice is safe before relying on it
Implementing a trie and using it for prefix search
Combining a hash map with a linked list for O(1) LRU eviction
Recognising monotonic stack problems from their wording
